title: [Proposal] A way to load parts of a page instead of the entire page.

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

labels.name: needs concrete proposal
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires someone to figure out a detailed plan

body:
Actually, changing URI context by clicking on a link will result in loading an entire page. Proposal. **Considere an HTML Document** ``` MY PAGE
LOGO AND PAGE TITLE HERE
LEFT COLUMN
Some content with a link : my link
RIGHT COLUMN
FOOTER
``` Note the hook attribute on some elements, and the `target=_hooks` on the link. **Let's take a look on a possible server response** ```
SUPER PAGE
NEW LEFT COLUMN
Come back to HOME
NEW FOOTER
``` **Desired result** ```
SUPER PAGE
NEW LEFT COLUMN
Come back to HOME
RIGHT COLUMN
NEW FOOTER
``` ### Technical points When clicking on the link, User Agent should indicates in the request header that web browser is fetching page parts and not the entire page. (For example : Content-Target: Hooks) If both server and browser support this feature, the page will not be entirely refreshed, but just the concerned parts. **Retro Copatibility** 1 - Server and browser don't support it The request header "Content-Target" will not be send and the server will send the entire page. The page will be entirely refreshed. 2 - Server support it, browser don't The request header "Content-Target" will not be send and the server will send the entire page. The page will be entirely refreshed. 3 - Browser support it, server don't The request header "Content-Target" will be send but the server will send the entire page. The browser will take the needed parts from the response with the help of the hook attribute values. The page will not be entirely refreshed, but just the concerned parts. **History API** If there is no use of preventDefault() function during the onClick event of the link, The URI context will be changed (address bar have to be updated too), and the previous state will be pushed to the History stack containing like this: ``` { "page-header" : " LOGO AND PAGE TITLE HERE ", "before-main": "LEFT COLUMN", "main" : "Some content with a link : my link", "after-main" : "RIGHT COLUMN", "page-footer" : "FOOTER" } ``` Note in this example, the right column is not given by the server, and this absence will be interpreted as "there is no change on this part" ### Conclusion This feature can be easily implemented by browsers and can provide a considerable optimisation without having to write any javascript code line. However, a javascript shim can easily be written in to make the User Agent supporting this feature.
